findings.text: Fix 2 breaks the "fallback wrote first" guarantee for a real tab. `RecordWriter.post` now sends `client` on every verb (`core/Item/RecordWriter.js:56`), but the stamped lines it hands back as `rest` for the fallback carry no `client` (line 51). So the line the tab appends through `Append.js` is keyed `owner|ts`, while the late post is checked with `c:<client>|ts` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:149`). They never match, the late post writes a second line, and `doc/one-writer.md:231` ("the late post is answered `{already: true}`") is no longer true. `one-writer.test.mjs:103` still passes only because its late verb is posted without a `client`, which no real tab does any more. The fix: put `client` on the verb lines in `list` too, so the fallback line carries it, and add a case 3 variant that uses the real tab shape.

Fix 1 says "newline guard before **every** append" (fixes.md 1), and `core/doc/status.md`'s Phase 0 row now says "Done". But only `RecordWriter.append_once` has the guard. The two main append paths still append blind: the entry point's `write_line` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:183`, used by every `record_lines` and item-tool write) and the dev server's fallback (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js:131`). Either add the guard there with a test, or change the status row to say what is really covered.

Fix 5 changes the on-disk shape of every browser `List.add`: fields now sit under `data` instead of flat (`core/List/List.js:254-263`). Nobody checked the readers that read an `add` payload flat instead of through `hydrate()`. Examples: `ai/rail/rail.js:484` (`fold.content?.add?.text ?? …title`), `ai/cards/Activity.js:143` and `ai/AISession/SessionTimelineRows.js:97`. A card added to a page's content list from the browser would now show blank in those summaries. Do the census, then fix each reader or say why it can't receive these lines.

The F4 helper is a static on `Runtime` (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Runtime.js:50`), and `rpc:write` is its only caller. fixes.md asks for "one crash-safe rewrite helper". Other rewriters still truncate in place: `Server/SessionConsolidate.mjs:110,132` uses plain `writeFileSync`. Consider moving the helper somewhere shared and listing its callers in status.md.

`safe_write` creates a `<file>.tmp-<pid>-<ms>` sibling inside the watched `public/` tree. LiveReload mutes only the real path (`Runtime.js:36`), so every save also queues a change for the tmp path, which is sent to every tab (`LiveReload.js:143-185`). That is probably harmless, because tabs ignore paths they didn't load, but it hasn't been checked.

Fix 2's second clause in fixes.md ("the item tool's own stamps repeat too (the flaky one-writer test)") is not addressed or mentioned. Fix 3 is marked "already built" with no test. The brief allows the skip, but status.md should link to the code that proves it (`ext/JSONL/live.js`, the `Socket.prototype.open` override).

Steps 2–8 (Ref/F7, Refs in `session.messages`, List-view hooks, `Sentence.at` + `Prompt.raw`, Prompt kind/items, session completion, the V1 compare) are not in it. findings.text: Step 2 asked for a census of every caller that `add`s an already-owned item, switching the ones that meant a move to `move_to`. The diff has no census file, no switched caller, and nothing in `s2/` mentions one. The rule is now live (`core/List/List.js`, `add()`) and any such caller silently gets a Ref instead of the item. Write the census into `s2/` (even if it is "none found") and link it from `core/List/readme.md`.

The diff has no test that fails on the old behaviour at a real caller. `List.test.mjs` proves `add()` makes a Ref, but nothing shows the existing callers still work. Add a line to the census saying which suites were run after F7 (the builder's `core/` tests, `chat-messages.test.mjs`, the one-writer suite) and their counts.

`Chat.resurface` (`core/Session/Chat/Chat.js`) builds the Ref with `this.add({type:"Ref", path})`, so it never goes through the F7 branch. Its comment says F7 "would only make a Ref anyway", which is true only for live items. The two-line "Ref's add, then original's set" is not atomic: a crash between them leaves a Ref with no `resurfaced` mark. Say so in `core/Item/doc/ref.md`, or write the mark first.

`core/Session/Chat/doc/views-on-messages.md` and `doc/pseudo-properties.md` do not mention `resurfaced`. dictation-v3 owns the views and needs to know the mark exists and what it means ("dim the original"). Add a line to `views-on-messages.md` and send them a short note.

`foreign_ref` in `List.js` takes `dest.owner ?? dest` for the root. An unowned list that is not yet attached would give the wrong root and wrongly treat a cross-file item as same-file. Worth a test for a detached list.
`add()` now returns the Ref, not the item. Callers that chain on the return value (`list.add(x).set(...)`) would now edit the Ref. The census in finding 1 should check for this too.
The `Chat.test.mjs` pass line says "15 checks", but the diff shows 13 asserts plus the earlier 7. Count it with the runner rather than by hand (Law 7).

A fresh agent can continue from `builder.md` and `plan.md`, which are clear. `s2/` holds only `past-work.md` and `session.jsonl`, with no summary of what step 2 decided. Step 3 would have to read the diff to learn that `add()` answers the Ref and that `Chat.js` imports `Ref.js`.

Requirements met for this step: F7, a Ref hydrating in `session.messages` and resurface all exist, each with a test. The `List` and `Chat` readmes and `ref.md` are updated. The "Next" list in the Chat readme is accurate.
